_readme: Hand-written copy. why: review whenever a country enters or leaves the dissident list (sync <= 3). myths: profiles of the artists dominating the consensus, kept manual because they need qualitative judgment the numbers don't give. Don't write numbers here; the page fills those in from data/latest.json.

br.story: Funk carioca and sertanejo generate more internal streams than any import could. The regional catalog isn't competing — it doesn't fit. It's the biggest market on the map and the most isolated one, at the same time.

mx.industry: Corridos tumbados and Mexican regional music
mx.story: The corridos tumbados revival and regional Mexican music fill the national chart before any consensus hit gets a look in. It's not the market's exception, it's the dominant industry.

do.story: Dembow has had its own production, DJ, and consumption infrastructure for over a decade. Some of the regional consensus gets in, but it's competing with a scene that doesn't need anyone's permission to fill a chart.

ar.story: RKT and Buenos Aires trap built their own production circuit starting in 2019. The scene doesn't chase the regional consensus — the consensus chases it. It tends to hover right around the dissident threshold.

KAROL G.world: She doesn't drop albums, she drops weather systems. Every project reconfigures the genre around her instead of joining it.
KAROL G.withheld: She rarely competes on the terrain of controversy. The absence of scandal is, itself, a brand decision.
KAROL G.risk: Dominating this many markets with one single exposes the whole catalog to a ceiling of familiarity: the consensus can turn predictable before it turns boring.

Bad Bunny.world: He doesn't drop albums, he drops weather systems. Every project reconfigures the genre around him instead of joining it.
Bad Bunny.withheld: Long silences between eras, a refusal to explain creative decisions at the moment he makes them. The mystery is part of the catalog.
Bad Bunny.risk: The risk isn't stream overexposure, it's premature canonization — when every move gets read as an era statement and there's no more room left to fail in public.

Omar Courtz.world: He builds on the recent Puerto Rican circuit without directly inheriting Bad Bunny's shadow: less world-narrative, more sound execution.
Omar Courtz.withheld: He hasn't had to carry a full era yet. The open question is whether KOKO is the start of a catalog or an isolated peak.
Omar Courtz.risk: Without a second move to confirm the first, the risk is getting read as one successful song instead of an artist with an arc.
